historic_survey.note: Named among the study area's extant historic automotive commercial resources, at 17th, Market and Collingwood streets. The statement dates the building 1933 in its property-type discussion and 1920 in a figure caption, and its industrial production framework concludes that the brief candy-making use and the building's adaptable functionality diminish its association with the history of industrial production in Eureka Valley.

historical_record.description: The partnership of McNaughton & Turner operated an automobile repair facility here.

Cora Lou Confectioners took over the repurposed automobile repair facility, moving from a previous location on Army Street. The firm specialised in marzipan and Danish confections and moved to 434 Castro Street some time in the mid-1950s.
The Board of Permit Appeals overruled the Police Department's denial of a permit for a place of entertainment at 2500 Market Street, with stipulations on hours, amplification and further permits.

The Board of Permit Appeals overruled the Police Department's denial of a request for modification of a stipulation on a permit for a place of entertainment at 2500 Market Street, modifying the stipulation so that there is no live entertainment after 1:30 a.m. on Thursday, Friday, and Saturday.
A currently closed athletic club occupied an existing vacant, two-story commercial building on the lot.
The City Planning Commission approved with conditions replacing a currently closed athletic club with one artist's live/work unit, 4-0.
The City Planning Commission approved with conditions using the existing structure as transitional housing for up to 15 homeless youths, 6-1.
